title: Product first, margins always
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you sell a product people love, or sell a product you hope they will buy?
Jose said the person asked his cousins: are you a sales organization, or are you focused on the product? In his head, the product comes first.

The cousins were proud that they were out selling, but it isn't sustainable unless you have a really good product, Jose said. There are two types of people: salespeople and product people. The clients will come if you have a good product. If you're selling without one, you get into danger.

groups.heading: A bottle that won a prize

lines.text: Jose told of an uncle who had a water-bottling plant. He won a prize in Europe for the best bottle, a hybrid between round and square. The water came from a family farm and was beautiful.

But when he went to distribute it to restaurants, he ran into a problem. A large soft-drink company has its own water brand and delivers twelve products on established trucks. A restaurant can't carry his water without asking the big company to take theirs out, and they won't.

A student said the person in the book is always thinking about the product and how to enhance it. Jose said: he is also thinking about the margins. One of the first things I ask about a business is: what are the margins?

His brother-in-law owned fast food franchises, which work on a five percent margin, he said. If you don't do something right, you're losing money. They work on volume. A bigger margin is a more forgiving business.

Sometimes you have a massive market share and low margins. Other times a small niche and a very high margin. In a business where the margin is small, you could be underwater by spending two or three hundred dollars more a month.
What is your margin, and what would break it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write whether you are a product person or a sales person.
Write your margin on one product.
Write the volume you need at that margin.
Write what stands between your product and your customer, like the trucks.

check.q: What did Jose say about a product and sales?
choices: The clients will come if you have a good product

check.q: What problem did the uncle's water have?
choices: Distribution, because a big company had the trucks

check.q: What did Jose say is a more forgiving business?

recap: Put the product first. Know your margin and your path to the customer.
